put.description: Display settings that follow the person to every device.

get.description: Starts the OIDC login in the browser. Navigate here; don't fetch it.

post.description: An OAuth token request (form: grant_type=authorization_code, code, code_verifier, redirect_uri, and optionally device_name) for a code from the IdP. Returns a bearer session as access_token.
Proves this server issued a bearer session, for the app checking a local address. Returns an HMAC-SHA256 of the nonce keyed by the SHA-256 of the session token. 404 for unknown sessions.
Ends this session. Then send the browser to endSessionUrl, when there is one, to sign out at the IdP as well; the IdP returns to the sign-in page (web) or to the app.

get.description: The items in a folder, or at the top of My files when folderId is left out.

post.description: Folder uploads: makes all the folders first, in one go, then the files are uploaded into them.

get.description: The original bytes, as an attachment. Supports ranges. Audited, unlike previews.
A WebP thumbnail of the file: small (256 px) for lists, medium (640 px) for the grid. 404 until the worker has made one; see NodeDto.thumbnail.

An audio file's loudness over time, for the player's timeline: a 16-byte header ("DKWF", version 1, three zero bytes, seconds per slice as float32, slice count as uint32, little-endian), then three bytes per slice: the lowest sample's size, the highest sample and the RMS, scaled so the loudest sample is 255. 404 until the worker has made one; see NodeDto.media.hasWaveform. Not audited.

What the viewer shows: a WebP for images browsers can't display or that are huge, the playable copy of a video or audio file browsers can't play (unless original=true), the PDF made of an Office document, otherwise the original bytes, inline. Supports ranges. Not audited, unlike downloads (§18).

A video's seek previews: one WebP of frames from along the video, laid out as NodeDto.media.seekPreviews says. 404 until the worker has made them, and for audio and clips under 10 s. Not audited, like previews.

post.description: Asks for a playable copy of a video or audio file browsers can't play, ahead of other work. 409 when copies are turned off or the file can't be converted; see NodeDto.media.

get.description: Where the worker is with the file's current version: thumbnail, metadata and text. Admins also get each failed step's job and error.

post.description: Run before uploading: which of these files (by SHA-256) the user already has.
Upload anyway: adds a file with content the user already has, without sending the bytes.

get.description: What the file's current version says about itself (title, date taken, camera, place…), with people's edits on top.

put.description: Edits the current version's title, description and date taken, all three at once; null keeps what the file says. Later versions start with these edits. The file itself is never changed.

get.description: The searchable text of the current version, page by page from `from`, with corrections in place.
The words recognized on one page of a scan or photo, with their boxes, for the viewer to show and select, and which pages have any. What was read, not corrections.

put.description: Corrects one page of the current version's text, or adds text to a page where none was read. Search uses it from then on.

delete.description: Drops a page's correction, so the text read from the file counts again.

post.description: Moves files and folders to the trash, folders with everything in them. Undo with /trash/restore.

get.description: What the user trashed, newest first. Things that went with a folder are counted in it, not listed.

post.description: Deletes items in the trash forever. Can't be undone.
Deletes everything in the trash forever. Can't be undone.
Stars files and folders for the person asking. Stars are each person's own.

get.description: What the person starred, trashed items left out. Unsorted: clients sort.

post.description: The viewer calls this when the person opens a file, for their Recent page. Private to them and not audited (§18).

get.description: The files the person last opened, downloaded, uploaded or restored a version of, newest first, at most 100.

Files and folders whose name, text or metadata match. `q` takes words, "exact phrases", -excluded words and the operators type:, in:, after:, before:, camera:, taken:, tag: and is:starred; the other parameters are the filter chips and override the operators. A word also finds files with a tag that has it.
Tags and name matches as someone types, best first.
The pages of one file that match `q`, for the viewer to open on and step through.
A file's tags, and the automatic tags someone took off it, for the details panel.

post.description: Adds and removes tags on one or more files at once. Removing an automatic tag is remembered for each file, so keyword rules don't add it back.

get.description: Tags on files the person can see, most used first, with how many files have each. `q` keeps those that start with it, or have a word that does.

post.description: Adds a rule at the end of the list: when one of your files gets the tag, it moves to the folder.

delete.description: Deletes a rule. Files it moved stay where they are.

put.description: Puts all your rules in this order. The first that matches a file wins.

post.description: How many of your files have the tag now and would be filed, with where a few would go. Changes nothing.

get.description: Files your rules moved after `after` (by default, the last two minutes) that are still there, oldest first.

post.description: Moves a filed file back where it was. No rule files it again.
Merges PDFs into one new file, in the order given. Answers at once; the worker puts the pages together, then the file appears. Follow it with GET /pdf/operations/{id}.
Splits a PDF into new files, one per part, next to it or in a new folder. Answers at once, like merging.

get.description: Your merges and splits from the last week, newest first.

delete.description: Stops a merge or split that hasn't saved anything yet.

post.description: A PDF's pages as small images, for choosing pages: says where each page is, and asks the worker to make them if they aren't made yet. 409 when the PDF can't be read or isn't processed yet.

get.description: One WebP sheet of page images, numbered from 1, laid out as RequestPageSheets says. Not audited, like previews.
For a file made by merging or splitting PDFs: what its current version was made from. 204 for other files.
What's said in a video or audio file, line by line with times.

post.description: Transcribes the file again from the start, ahead of the background work, e.g. after the admin picked another model. The old transcript stays until the new run starts. 409 when the file isn't transcribed (no sound, speech to text off, or no ML service).

get.description: The transcript as WebVTT captions, for the player's CC button. 404 until there is one.
The state of a tus upload, and once complete, the file it produced and any duplicates of it.

put.description: Turning it on reads again, in the background, the files skipped while it was off.

post.description: Reads the text of every stored file again, in the background, after new files are done.

get.description: Checks every saved ML service now.
How many playable copies of videos exist, the disk they take, and how many are still to make.

delete.description: Deletes every playable copy. The originals are untouched; copies are made again as the setting says.

put.description: Turning it on, or including videos, queues the recordings not transcribed yet, in the background.

post.description: Transcribes every stored recording again, in the background, e.g. after picking another model. Old transcripts stay searchable until each is redone.

put.description: Paused queues start no new jobs; running ones finish.

get.description: Running jobs longest-running first, queued ones in the order they will run, failed ones latest first.

post.description: Every failed job, or those of one type, with fresh attempts.

delete.description: Forgets a failed job without running it again.

post.description: Adds a rule and runs it over every stored file in the background.

put.description: Changing the tag or words runs the rule again over every file in the background; turning it off takes its tags off at once.

delete.description: Deletes the rule and takes its tags off every file.

post.description: How many files a rule would tag, and which, a page at a time. Changes nothing.
